# Draft:Office of the President of the Czech Republic

The Office of the President of the Czech Republic also known as the Chancellery of the President of the Republic (, KPR) is an institution that assists the President of the Czech Republic with fulfilling his tasks as head of state. The original Czechoslovak Presidential Office was established in 1919, and after the dissolution of Czechoslovakia, the Czech Presidential Office followed suit in 1993. It is located at Prague Castle and is led by a head (unofficially called the Chancellor), who has been Milan Vašina since February 2024.

Organization
The Office of the President of the Republic is an organizational unit of the state and a budgetary organization with a separate chapter in the state budget of the Czech Republic.  The employees of the Office of the President of the Republic are in regular employment and do not fall under the civil service .
The Office ensures the provision of matters related to the exercise of the powers of the President of the Republic, which are stipulated by law, with protocol duties and public activities of the President of the Republic. It also manages the real estate, consisting of the Prague Castle complex and the Lány Chateau , and movable property related to these properties or the activities of the KPR itself. The Office has the authority to establish contributory organizations to manage real estate .  In 1993, two such organizations were established, namely the Prague Castle Administration and the Lány Forest Administration .
The Office of the President of the Republic is located at Prague Castle in the New Royal Palace . It is headed by the Head of the Office,  informally called the Chancellor,  who is appointed and dismissed by the President of the Republic.
The Office of the President of the Republic includes two specialized archives, the Archives of the Office of the President of the Republic and the Archives of the Prague Castle .
Chiefs of the Chancellery
In the years 1919–1968, he was the head, in 1969–1970, the state secretary to the President of the Republic, and since 1970, the head.
